title: Investing Is Compression
abstract: arXiv:2604.10758v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: In 1956 John Kelly wrote a paper at Bell Labs describing the relationship between gambling and Information Theory. What came to be known as the Kelly Criterion is both an objective and a closed-form solution to sizing wagers when odds and edge are known. Samuelson argued it was arbitrary and subjective, and successfully kept it out of mainstream economics. Luckily it lived on in computer science, mostly because of Tom Cover's work at Stanford. He showed that it is the uniquely optimal way to invest: it maximizes long-term wealth, minimizes the risk of ruin, and is competitively optimal in a game-theoretic sense, even over the short term. translated_abstract: 1956年，John Kelly在贝尔实验室撰写了一篇论文，描述了赌博与信息论之间的关系。后来被称为凯利公式的理论，是在赔率和优势已知时确定下注规模的客观且具有闭式解的方法。Samuelson认为它是任意和主观的，并成功将其排除在主流经济学之外。幸运的是，它在计算机科学中得以延续，这主要归功于Tom Cover在斯坦福大学的工作。他证明了这是唯一最优的投资方式：它使长期财富最大化，使破产风险最小化，并且在博弈论意义上具有竞争最优性，即使在短期内也是如此。Cover对投资组合理论最令人惊讶的贡献之一是通用投资组合。它与信息论中的通用压缩相关，其渐近表现与事后来看最优的恒定再平衡投资组合一样好。我借用了该算法的一个技巧来证明凯利……
tldr: 本文追溯了凯利公式从被Samuelson排除于主流经济学到在计算机科学中经由Tom Cover工作而复兴的历程，并借鉴通用投资组合（与通用压缩相关）的算法技巧，论证投资本质上就是压缩。
en_tdlr: This paper traces the Kelly Criterion's journey from being excluded from mainstream economics by Samuelson to its revival in computer science through Tom Cover's work, and borrows a trick from the universal portfolio algorithm (related to universal compression) to argue that investing is essentially compression.
